title: Linear bandits with parameter noise, known covariance, and a p-norm ball
summary: Each round draws a fresh random parameter vector, and the learner observes only its exact projection along the selected action. Actions lie in the unit p-norm ball. Noise variance depends jointly on the direction and the public covariance matrix.

model.instance: $$\mathcal A=\{a\in\mathbb R^d:\|a\|_p\le1\},\qquad 1<p\le2,\qquad q=\frac{p}{p-1}.$$ $$\theta_t\overset{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}\sim\nu,\qquad \mathbb E\theta_t=\theta_*,\qquad \operatorname{Cov}(\theta_t)=\Sigma,\qquad |\langle a,\theta_t\rangle|\le1\quad\text{almost surely, for every }a\in\mathcal A.$$ Randomness comes from a fresh parameter vector each round; the feedback is not a linear regression observation with additive homoscedastic scalar noise. $$N=T,\qquad \sigma_q^2=\left(\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Sigma_{ii}^{q/2}\right)^{2/q}.$$ Here $N$ counts scalar observations. The quantity $\sigma_q^2$ is defined by the covariance diagonal and cannot be replaced by the maximum action variance.

model.parameter_domain_description: T: $T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1$ (public); d: $d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge1$ (public); \delta_{\mathrm{conf}}: $0<\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}<1$ (public); p: $1<p\le2$ (public); q: $q=p/(p-1)\in[2,\infty)$ (public); \Sigma: $\Sigma\in\mathbb R^{d\times d},\ \Sigma\succeq0$ (public); \sigma_q^2: $\sigma_q^2\ge0$ (public)

operations.query_signature: $$Y_t=\langle a_t,\theta_t\rangle,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(Y_t\mid a_t)=a_t^{\mathsf T}\Sigma a_t.$$ Choose $a_t$ first, then draw a fresh $\theta_t$ and reveal only the scalar projection. The same $\theta_t$ defines all counterfactual rewards that round, but other projections are hidden. Causal policies are allowed. Inputs $d,p,q,T,\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}$ and covariance $\Sigma$ are public; the distribution $\nu$ and mean $\theta_*$ are hidden. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally; no unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available. Within-round exceptions require explicit full-function or common-sample access.
